codeReview.summary: The NewsletterEditor component is well-implemented. It correctly creates a TipTap rich text editor with all required extensions (StarterKit, TextStyle, Color, Highlight), a complete formatting toolbar (Bold, Italic, Underline, Text Color, Highlight, H2, H3, Bullet List, Link, Undo, Redo), a ClearableInput for the heading field defaulting to the store value, and a Top/Bottom position toggle. Editor content syncs to store.newsletterBody on every change. 27 unit tests cover rendering, toolbar interactions, heading input, position toggle, and active states. The component follows project conventions (Tailwind-only styling, path aliases, shadcn/ui components). The component itself does not wrap in CollapsibleCard (correctly — that's the integration feature's responsibility). XSS paste sanitization was added in a subsequent commit (cb9d761) which is the correct scope separation.

issues.description: The ColorInput component uses document.querySelector with a data attribute to find the hidden color input, which is fragile if multiple instances exist. The NewsletterEditor is only used once so this is not a practical issue, but it would be cleaner to use a ref.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a React ref forwarded to the hidden input element instead of document.querySelector.

issues.description: The useCallback hooks for handleHeadingChange and handlePositionChange depend on [store] (the entire store object), which will cause them to re-create on every store change since usePromotionStore() returns a new object reference each time. In practice this has no performance impact since these are only passed to a ClearableInput and Button components, but it's technically unnecessary.
issues.suggestedFix: Destructure specific actions from usePromotionStore: const setNewsletterHeading = usePromotionStore(s => s.setNewsletterHeading); and use those directly instead of wrapping in useCallback.

issues.description: The link handler uses window.prompt() which works but is not accessible or customizable. A future enhancement could use a proper dialog/popover component for URL input.
issues.suggestedFix: Consider using a shadcn/ui Dialog or Popover for URL input in a future iteration.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The TipTap editor requires immediatelyRender: false for SSR/JSDOM compatibility. This is a TipTap-specific requirement that's not documented in the mission AGENTS.md but was correctly applied by the worker.
sharedStateObservations.suggestedContent: Add to TipTap coding conventions: 'TipTap useEditor() must use immediatelyRender: false for JSDOM test compatibility.'

sharedStateObservations.observation: The worker correctly separated the XSS sanitization (SanitizePasteExtension) into the newsletter-card-integration feature rather than including it in the editor component. This shows good scope discipline — the editor component focuses on editing, while the integration handles security sanitization. The later commit (cb9d761) added the paste extension properly.
sharedStateObservations.suggestedContent: Document that XSS paste sanitization for TipTap is handled via a custom Extension (SanitizePasteExtension) registered in the editor's extensions array. This pattern can be reused for any TipTap editor in the project.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The feature description mentions '8 format types' for the toolbar but the actual toolbar has 10 buttons (Undo, Redo, Bold, Italic, Underline, Text Color, Highlight, H2, H3, Bullet List, Link) plus 2 color pickers. The implementation correctly includes Undo/Redo in addition to the 8 formatting types. The expectedBehavior list also includes 'Undo/redo works' as a separate criterion. This is not a bug — just a minor description ambiguity.
sharedStateObservations.suggestedContent: No action needed — the expectedBehavior list is the source of truth and is unambiguous.

summary: The NewsletterEditor component (commit 73b49a7) is a clean, well-structured implementation that fully satisfies its feature requirements. All 14 expected behavior criteria are met: TipTap editor with correct extensions, complete toolbar with active state tracking, heading input with ClearableInput, position toggle, store sync on every change, undo/redo via keyboard shortcuts, and support for multiple simultaneous formats. The component properly defers CollapsibleCard wrapping and XSS sanitization to the integration feature (cb9d761), demonstrating good scope separation. 27 unit tests pass covering rendering, interactions, and state management. Two non-blocking issues noted (document.querySelector in ColorInput, useCallback dependency on full store object) and one suggestion (window.prompt → Dialog). Status: PASS.
